newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan to let firms buy back 10 pct of own stock.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan to let firms buy back 10 pct of own stock.

text.p: Pakistan's caretaker cabinet decided on Monday to allow companies to repurchase up to 10 percent of their own shares as part of measures to stimulate the country's three stock markets, a government official said.

Shahid Javed Burki, finance and economic affairs adviser to the prime minister, told a news conference that bonus shares would be exempted from withholding tax, and earnings from rights issues would be exempted from income tax.

"Not only will this be helpful to the corporate sector, but this will put capital market development on the right track," Burki said as he unveiled a package of incentives aimed at reviving sentiment at Pakistan's sagging bourses.
He said the government had asked the four provincial governments to rationalise stamp duty on share transactions and reduce it to the level now applicable in Sindh province.
Burki said companies who wished to repurchase treasury stock would have to announce their intentions through a tender offer published in newspapers in a timely manner.
He said the package had been approved after consultation with the presidents and directors of the Karachi, Lahore and Islamabad stock exchanges.
